title: Global dynamics and regime shifts in a resource-consumer model with facilitation and habitat loss
summary: Modelling how populations respond to habitat loss is crucial for understanding ecosystem stability, especially when positive interactions among resource species, such as plant-plant facilitation, play a key role. Habitat loss not only reduces available organic nutrients and space for primary producers but also disrupts the positive feedbacks that sustain resource populations, thereby affecting consumer persistence and the overall system's stability.
